The game

The first island. You land with nothing: pick up branches and stones at camp and make your first tools by hand, chop and mine, build a hut, put a workbench under its roof, hunt the boar for meat and hide, and come back to it all later: the game saves itself. Esc has restart and a sandbox.

Controls

WASD
Walk. Hold Shift to sprint
J or Left click
Swing the sword or the tool, or shoot the bow. Hold for a charged swing
K or Right click
Block. Press just before a hit to parry
Space
Dash
1 to 6
Take the thing in that slot of the bar in hand, or use it (food, a torch); its number again puts it away. The bar is the bag's top row: drag things into it. An axe, a pick, a knife or a rod in hand gathers; anything else, or empty hands, fights. The right tool does full damage, the wrong one half
Ctrl
Target the nearest beast; again for the next, then let go
X
Draw your weapon, or put it away. Among other people it is away until you draw it, and a drawn blade is a threat
Esc
Closes whatever board is open; else the menu: continue, a sandbox to try things out in, restart with nothing or a new island (each asks for a second click), the music and the sounds of the world
B
Build mode. The Building board opens with it, and again on Right click: a tab for walls, floors and roofs, ground, yard, furniture, work and outdoors, every piece with its name and what it costs. Pick one, then click to place it (drag for walls and floors). F turns the cursor into the wreck cursor: the piece under it glows, and a click takes it down and gives the material back
Mouse wheel
Pick a slot on the bar (Enter takes the pick in hand, or puts it away; a number key does the same for its slot); in build mode through the pieces you know (it turns a thing you are about to set down), and over the Building board through its tabs
E
Use what you face: a workbench, a hearth or a furnace (its board; E again closes it), a bed from dusk (sleep until morning), a chest (opens beside the bag), a seat, a boat, a cave, a person to talk to, berries to pick. The words over the hero say what it will do
In the bag
Drag a thing to move it; off the boards, to lay it on the ground (a weapon or a tool lies there until E takes it up again). Right click uses it: eats a food, lights a torch, sends a weapon or a tool to its bar, puts a garment on (on the character panel, takes it off). Shift and click sends it across to an open chest, or out of one. Shift and drag carries half a stack
Tab
The one screen: your panel top left (the hero and what is worn; pages for the numbers and the ring come as you earn them), the bag under it, and on the right what you can make where you stand (by hand, or the bench, hearth or furnace beside you): six slots wide, stacks of 25, its top two rows the Fight bar and the Gather bar. Point at a thing for its card. Sort tidies the rows below the bars
R
Rise again after you have fallen

What there is to do

Trees take a few chops with the axe and fall. Rocks crack as you mine them and break apart. Bushes are cut with the knife. What falls out lies on the ground until you walk over it, and lands in your inventory.

The bow shoots without arrows for now (the quiver is gone until a better way of carrying arrows is found).

Young boars, deer and adders live on the starter island; on the big island grown boars, moose and bears too, and a troll in his cave. They keep to their home ranges and leave you alone until you come close; the deer go in herds and run, the rest charge. A deer you have shot bleeds: follow the blood. At night a pack of wolves comes, and a fire keeps it off. Meat and hide from most; antler from the moose. Berry bushes give berries.

Somewhere inland is a broken steading: a burnt hall, a hut still standing, a plank house by the well with its walls broken and its roof gone (mend it, and it is your first home), a palisade with gaps, crates with things left behind (break them open with the axe), and Arnor the smith by the well, who will tell you what happened. The pieces are the same you build with, and the wreck cursor takes them apart for their wood and stone. A chest you build holds twelve stacks.

Food never punishes you: you do not have to eat. Eat, and you heal; cook a meal at the hearth and your health keeps coming back for minutes, with your top health raised. Roast boar is good; boar and berry stew is better. Open the bag and right click food to eat it, or put it on the bar and press its number.

Building is cheap: a wall, door or window costs two wood (a stone wall two stone), a floor tile one wood, and a hearth of your own four stone and two wood (you can cook at it like the one at camp). Close a loop of walls and a thatch roof appears by itself, and fades when you step inside. Add a door, or you will not get in.

Your island, inventory, buildings and felled trees are saved in this browser and are there when you come back. "New island" throws it all away and starts again.

The chart in the corner shows the island; the yellow dot is you.
